successes: wealth: financial resources, not methods, in both final runs.
endorsement: withheld formal approval without inventing a rejection.
orwell-1946: correctly preserved language affecting thought after baseline wrong-direction answer.
sarcasm: correctly identified ironic displeasure in both final runs.
powder-literal and new-literal-ice: physical interpretation in both final runs.
heldout-metaphor, new-litotes, new-restive, new-heavy-lifting: useful core sense in both final runs.
remainingFailures: ambiguity: asserted the man held the telescope in both final runs; omitted observer using it.
new-duck: asserted an owned bird in both final runs; omitted watching a woman duck.
heldout-cat: secret-disclosure interpretation persisted despite the animal running under a sofa, both final runs.
heldout-wanting: said absent rather than deficient in both final runs. Dictionary-assisted v2 corrected this.
agreement: terminated can imply a completed agreement being ended rather than one failing to materialize; assisted v2 was clearer.
powder-figurative: attributed the belief to Eleanor, but narrowed preparedness to objections/arguments and omitted keeping options ready.
almost-convincing: treated lack of sincerity as fact rather than an implication of apparently unconvincing enthusiasm.
understatement: understood deficient manners but did not explain the formal understatement well.
sealioning: no invented seal-origin story after baseline, but descriptions omit some defining features and can still overstate intent.
manualReview.dictionaryTradeoff: Assisted v2 supplied exact fall-through evidence and corrected wanting. It also invented unlocking/unlatching for opened and reinforced the cat idiom error. Assistance stays optional and defaults off.
